title: Coffee & Tree Café
description: A café and covered promenade threaded through the landscape of Bailuwan Town. Its vivid structure and lightweight canopy turn an everyday path into a social space shaped around trees, shade and movement.

title: The Henderson
description: A sculpted office tower rising from Hong Kong’s dense Central district. The photographs follow its reflective form through compressed streets, tram lines and the layered public interiors at its base.

title: Expo Cultural Park Greenhouse Garden
description: A family of glazed greenhouse volumes set within Shanghai Expo Culture Park. Lightweight steel frames, circular roof openings and planted interiors transform a former industrial landscape into a sequence of climatic gardens.

title: Parkview Green
description: A mixed-use complex enclosed by a vast environmental envelope. Bridges, art, retail and circulation overlap inside the atrium, producing a compact interior city protected from Beijing’s climate.

title: Nanjing Constitution Park
description: A civic landscape composed through circles, axial courts and reflective water. The restrained palette gives the public complex a ceremonial character while keeping the sequence open to everyday movement.

title: Sifang Art Museum
architect: Steven Holl Architects and other architects
description: A hovering gallery volume turns toward the distant city above a dark concrete base. The museum’s shifting perspective connects close woodland, water and the skyline beyond.

title: National Museum of Western Art
description: Le Corbusier’s museum in Ueno Park is organized around a square central hall and a spiralling route of galleries. Its modular concrete façade and carefully controlled daylight give the building a quiet, enduring presence.

title: China Academy of Art, Liangzhu Campus
description: A design campus conceived as a community of workshops, streets and shared courtyards. Repeated arches, bridges and robust building volumes create a flexible framework for learning and daily life.

title: China Academy of Art, Xiangshan Campus
architect: Amateur Architecture Studio — Wang Shu & Lu Wenyu
description: A campus built as a loose settlement around Xiangshan Hill. Reused tiles, deep roofs, bridges and courtyards combine regional building memory with a contemporary academic landscape.

title: Zaishui Art Museum
description: An exceptionally long, low roof traces the surface of an artificial lake. Water enters the interior and the boundary between gallery, landscape and reflection is reduced to a line of slender columns and glass.

title: Tianjin Library
description: A monumental library organized as a layered public interior. Reading rooms, bridges and walls of books gather around luminous voids, balancing the scale of an institution with the intimacy of study.

title: OōEli
description: A mixed-use urban block shaped by porous courtyards, shaded passages and planted roofs. The ensemble opens a calm pedestrian interior within Hangzhou’s dense city fabric.

title: UCCA Clay Museum
description: A museum for Yixing’s ceramic culture formed by undulating walls clad in handmade tiles. The curved masonry gathers visitors into shaded courts while making clay itself the architecture’s dominant surface.

title: Start Museum
description: An industrial structure on the former railway site is retained and adapted as a contemporary art museum. Long platforms, cranes and new galleries preserve the memory of movement along the riverfront.

title: Hangzhou Prism
description: A mixed-use building cut by oblique terraces and a large interior void. The folded façade turns a conventional urban block into a shifting field of light, depth and framed views.

title: Hangzhou National Version Museum
architect: Amateur Architecture Studio — Wang Shu & Lu Wenyu
description: Wenrun Pavilion is set into a former quarry as a sequence of halls, gardens and covered walks. Stone, timber and translucent screens give the national archive the atmosphere of a contemporary Jiangnan landscape.

title: Grand Canal Hanggang Park
description: A former steelworks is reopened as a public landscape while blast furnaces, conveyors and workshops remain legible. New paths and cultural programs move through the industrial fabric without erasing its scale or material weight.

title: Forest Kindergarten
description: A continuous, almost weightless roof spreads across the ground like an abstract landscape. Openings, thin columns and changing ceiling heights create an environment that is closer to a forest floor than a conventional school building.

title: Qintai Art Museum
description: A museum whose folded roof continues the surrounding park. Ramps, planted terraces and white aggregate surfaces allow visitors to move across the building as part of the public landscape.

title: Sanhe House
architect: Amateur Architecture Studio — Wang Shu & Lu Wenyu
description: Three house-like volumes gather around water and mature trees. Curving concrete roofs and grey walls reinterpret the spatial intimacy of a traditional courtyard without reproducing its historical form.

title: Bailuwan Technology & Finance Town
description: A compact low-rise district articulated by white volumes, narrow lanes and deep geometric openings. Repetition and strong shadows give the working town the atmosphere of an abstract village.

title: Bailuwan Cultural Center
description: A cultural pavilion dissolved into a field of slender columns, water and trees. A broad translucent roof filters daylight while paths pass continuously between interior rooms and planted courts.

title: Tong Jun Residence
description: The architect Tong Jun designed this modest family house in 1947. Its domestic rooms, furniture and recent museum use offer an unusually intimate view of a foundational figure in modern Chinese architecture.

title: MIHO Museum
architect: I. M. Pei / Pei Cobb Freed & Partners
description: Reached through a tunnel and suspension bridge, the museum is embedded in the wooded mountains of Shiga. Geometric glass roofs and warm stone interiors frame a carefully choreographed arrival through landscape.

title: Liangzhu Cultural Arts Centre
description: Known locally as The Roof, the cultural centre gathers a library, galleries and learning spaces beneath one broad concrete plane. The interior is cut by circular stairs and quiet shafts of daylight.

title: Liangzhu Big Barn
description: A steeply pitched cultural building conceived as a contemporary storehouse for books and ideas. Its simple silhouette joins concrete, dark metal and a generous public interior.

title: H+ Art Museum
description: A compact private museum organized as a three-dimensional garden. Stepped volumes, fair-faced concrete, glazed planes and roof terraces create a slow sequence of changing viewpoints beside Suzhou’s old city.

title: Suzhou Museum of Contemporary Art
description: A chain of pavilion-like volumes follows the edge of Jinji Lake beneath a continuous folded roof. The museum is conceived as both an exhibition building and a new public promenade.

title: Suzhou Museum of Imperial Kiln Brick
description: The museum and kiln-ruins park are built from brick, concrete and recovered industrial fragments. Deep passages and monumental walls translate the process of making imperial bricks into spatial experience.

title: Shishan Grand Theatre
description: A group of translucent, gently curved volumes sits beside the water at Shishan Cultural Square. The light roofline breaks down the scale of the performing arts complex and reflects the surrounding landscape.

title: Suzhou Science and Technology Museum
description: A long, floating roof draws on silk, water and the form of a jade ruyi. The museum folds around courtyards and lakefront public space, connecting exhibition routes with the landscape of Shishan.

title: TAG Art Museum
description: A waterfront museum made from contrasting halls, courtyards and long horizontal windows. Framed views of sea, grasses and distant city become part of the exhibition sequence.

title: Jinji Station No. 9
description: A small lakeside pavilion related to the nearby contemporary art museum. Its dark folded profile extends the larger project’s roof language at the scale of a public stop along the Jinji Lake promenade.

title: Huanglong Mountain Zisha Mineral Source Museum
architect: Architecture School of Southeast University + Atelier XÜK
description: A museum and protected mine site dedicated to the mineral source of Yixing zisha clay. Ceramic façade pieces give the new volumes a changing, glaze-like surface tied directly to the material being exhibited.

title: Long Museum West Bund
description: A former coal-hopper structure is absorbed into a sequence of umbrella-like concrete vaults. Old infrastructure, new galleries and the open riverfront remain visible together rather than being separated into different eras.

title: Modum Atelier Nanjing Office
description: Modum Atelier's Nanjing office adapts a row-house unit in National Leading Talents Pioneer Park, formerly part of the late-Qing Jiangnan minting bureau. The renovation balances old and new construction while softening the boundary between workplace, domestic life and the surrounding lane.
